overview: The School Committee held a public hearing on the Superintendent’s $90.6 million FY27 preliminary operating budget, which identifies a $4 million increase over the previous year. The committee approved the budget proposal and a request for city free cash while highlighting a remaining $2 million gap between school needs and the city target.

items.title: FY27 Preliminary Operating Budget Presentation
items.summary: Finance staff presented a revised budget that reduced a projected $7.4 million increase to $4 million through enrollment-based staffing shifts, deferring leadership positions to FY28, and utilizing alternative revenue sources like circuit breakers. The proposal prioritizes collective bargaining obligations and special education mandates while funding a new middle school ELA curriculum.

items.title: Committee Discussion on Staffing and Capital Needs
items.summary: Members expressed concern over the deferral of an inclusion specialist and a network director, while the administration cited hiring difficulties and internal restructuring as factors. The committee requested a comprehensive budget appendix listing every position funded through revolving accounts to ensure transparency regarding the true cost of operations.

items.title: Budget Gap and City Fiscal Constraints
items.summary: The committee discussed a $2 million variance between the school department's request and the city's funding target. Mayor Lungo-Koehn indicated that while the city is seeking additional funds, rising health insurance costs and infrastructure debt will likely require reductions on both the municipal and school sides.

items.title: Approval of FY27 Budget Recommendations
items.summary: Approved recommendations for the general fund appropriation, a stabilization fund transfer, and a free cash request for capital maintenance needs including hot water tank and AED replacements. The motion included a priority to reinstate the inclusion specialist position as soon as funding allows.
